skill.name: jira-cli
skill.description: Interact with Jira from the command line to create, list, view, edit, and transition issues, manage sprints and epics, and perform common Jira workflows. Use when the user asks about Jira tasks, tickets, issues, sprints, or needs to manage project work items.
skill.summary: Use jira-cli commands to manage Jira issues, epics, sprints, boards, and project workflows.
skill.author: Code-and-Sorts

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are markdown examples for jira-cli, not executable code embedded in the skill. Real residual risk comes from guiding an agent to run an external CLI that can read and mutate Jira data. No prompt injection or covert exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Destructive Jira operations lack explicit confirmation guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Require a preview and user confirmation before delete, transition, assignment, comment, worklog, clone, or link commands.

remediation.issue: External CLI execution can affect the wrong Jira project or site.
remediation.suggestion: Instruct agents to confirm the Jira site, active project, and issue key before running write operations.

remediation.issue: API token setup guidance is brief.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to store JIRA_API_TOKEN securely and never paste tokens into prompts, comments, or issue descriptions.

semantic_findings.title: Destructive Jira Operations Lack Guardrails
semantic_findings.description: The skill documents write and delete commands, including issue transitions, comments, worklogs, linking, cloning, and deletion, without requiring explicit confirmation before irreversible changes. This can cause unintended Jira workflow changes when an agent executes the examples with valid credentials.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited sections contain concrete commands that move, log work, link, clone, and delete Jira issues. The risk is business-logic impact rather than code execution, so confidence is high but not critical.

content.user_title: Manage Jira Workflows from the CLI
content.value_statement: Teams lose time switching between Jira screens and development tools. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through jira-cli commands for common issue, sprint, and epic work.
actual_capabilities: List Jira issues by assignee, status, priority, JQL, and creation date.
Create bugs, stories, tasks, labels, components, and self-assigned issues.
View issues with comments, plain text output, and browser opening.
Edit summaries, descriptions, priorities, labels, assignments, comments, worklogs, and workflow states.
Manage epics, sprints, boards, projects, releases, and shell completion.
limitations: Requires jira-cli installed and configured with jira init.
Requires a valid JIRA_API_TOKEN and Jira account permissions.
Custom fields may need explicit field IDs and custom options.
Behavior can vary between Jira Cloud and Jira Server instances.

use_cases.title: Review Assigned Work
use_cases.description: List current Jira issues, filter by status or priority, and open the needed ticket details.

use_cases.title: Track Sprint Progress
use_cases.description: Check active sprint issues, move work through statuses, and summarize blockers for standup.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Epics and Releases
use_cases.description: List epics, attach issues, inspect releases, and export concise project progress summaries.

prompt_templates.title: List My Open Issues
prompt_templates.prompt: Show my Jira issues in the current project, grouped by status. Use plain text output when possible.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Bug
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a high priority Jira bug for a login crash. Include a concise summary, reproduction notes, and a bug label.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Sprint Work
prompt_templates.prompt: Find my current sprint issues, identify blockers from issue summaries and comments, and suggest the next three actions.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Issue Cleanup
prompt_templates.prompt: Search for high priority issues created this week, summarize them, and prepare safe update commands for my approval.

output_examples.output: A concise list of assigned sprint issues with keys, summaries, statuses, and next actions.

output_examples.input: Create a task for dependency updates.
output_examples.output: A confirmation-ready issue draft with type, summary, priority, labels, and component details.

output_examples.input: Summarize high priority bugs from this week.
output_examples.output: A short report of matching issues with owners, status, age, and recommended follow-up steps.

best_practices: Confirm the active project and Jira site before creating or editing issues.
Use plain text or CSV output for summaries and reports.
Ask for explicit approval before deleting issues or closing work.
anti_patterns: Do not run destructive commands without a clear issue key and user confirmation.
Do not paste API tokens into prompts or ticket comments.
Do not rely on default Jira project settings when multiple projects are configured.

faq.question: What does this skill require?
faq.answer: It requires jira-cli, a configured Jira account, and a valid JIRA_API_TOKEN.

faq.question: Can it create and edit Jira issues?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents commands for creating, editing, assigning, commenting, and transitioning issues.

faq.question: Does it support sprint and epic workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes commands for listing sprints, adding issues to sprints, and managing epics.

faq.question: Can it export issue data?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows plain text, raw, and CSV output modes for reports and scripting.

faq.question: Does it work with every Jira instance?
faq.answer: Most commands are standard, but custom fields and Jira Server behavior can vary.

faq.question: How should destructive actions be handled?
faq.answer: Preview the command, verify the issue key, and get explicit user approval before execution.
